_comment: Real declared/inferred ligand pairs from the DDD corpus, read off disk on
[[ligands]].smiles that fix_ligand_smiles.py filled from the PDBbind
reference table; 'inferred' is what mol_id.py perceived from the
simulation's own coordinates and recorded in
ligand_check.check() returns for the pair, measured, not predicted.
No contributor data here -- chemistry only.

cases.why: The central case. Sulfonic acid perceived from coordinates as three single-bonded hydroxyls: same skeleton, two hydrogens apart. Publishes.
cases.detail: ligand[0] formula (C14H8O5S vs C14H10O5S), hydrogen attachment

cases.why: Stereo-only difference, nothing else moving. Progesterone, declared flat, perceived with full tetrahedral stereo. The 22.2% class.
Fragment artifact: a phosphonate whose P-C bond was cut. Every atom present, bond graph split. Cleared by the 2026-09-04 revision.
cases.detail: ligand[0] split bond graph, all atoms present (OP(=O)=O)

cases.why: Fragment artifact of the simplest kind: a detached H2. Also cleared 2026-09-04.
The boundary. Looks like a fragment artifact -- a detached ammonia -- but four hydrogens are genuinely adrift, so the rescue must NOT fire. Its block stands.
cases.detail: ligand[0] connectivity differs, formula C20H17N5O vs C20H21N5O

cases.why: A genuinely different molecule. The reference table's ligand name disagrees with the metadata's, and the coordinates side with the metadata. This is the case --allow-name-mismatch would publish wrongly.
cases.detail: ligand[0] connectivity differs, formula C4H10O2S2 vs C10H14

cases.why: The RDKit fallback case. Its inferred side carries a neutral four-bonded nitrogen ([NH3]), which RDKit refuses, so the whole pair is computed with OpenBabel instead. The verdict is unaffected.
cases.detail: ligand[0] formula (C23H27N3O6S vs C23H28N3O6S), hydrogen attachment, tetrahedral stereo
